code.title: My First C++ Greeting
code.description:
Every C++ journey starts with a structured program. Write a program that prints a three-line welcome banner exactly as shown.

Input Format:
No input.

Output Format:
====================
Hello from C++
ATOM CODE
====================

Constraints:
None.

code.title: Welcome Note Printer
code.description:
A workshop registration desk greets every participant with a printed note. Read the participant's name (a single word) and age (an integer), then print the note.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: name (single word) and age (integer).

Output Format:
Welcome, <name>!
Age group: <age>

Constraints:
1 <= age <= 100

code.title: Variable Value Mirror
code.description:
To understand how different data types are stored, read one integer, one double and one character, then print each with a label.

Input Format:
One line with three tokens: an integer, a double and a single character separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Integer: <int>
Decimal: <double>
Symbol: <char>

Constraints:
-1000 <= integer <= 1000, 0 <= double <= 9999

code.title: Rectangle Area Calculator
code.description:
A civil drafting student measures a rectangular plot. Read the width and height in metres (integers) and print the area and the perimeter.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: width and height.

Output Format:
Area: <width * height>
Perimeter: <2 * (width + height)>

Constraints:
1 <= width, height <= 10000

code.title: Circle Area with Constant PI
code.description:
Declare a constant PI = 3.14159 and use it to compute the area of a circle. Read the radius (an integer) and print the area rounded down to the nearest whole square unit.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: radius.

Output Format:
Exact area: <PI * r * r>
Whole area: <integer part of the area>

Constraints:
1 <= radius <= 1000

code.title: Character Echo Box
code.description:
Computers store characters as numbers. Read a single character and print it together with its integer (ASCII) code and the character that follows it in the ASCII table.

Input Format:
One line with one character.

Output Format:
Char: <c>
Code: <ascii value>
Next: <c + 1 as character>

Constraints:
Input character is a printable ASCII character (code 33 to 125).

code.title: Movie Ticket Total
code.description:
A cinema box office sells tickets at a fixed price each. Read the price of one ticket (integer rupees) and the number of tickets bought (integer), then print the amount payable.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: ticket price and ticket count.

Output Format:
Tickets: <count>
Amount payable: <price * count> rupees

Constraints:
1 <= ticket price <= 1000, 1 <= ticket count <= 50

code.title: Cafeteria Bill
code.description:
The college cafeteria charges per plate. Read the price of one plate (integer rupees) and the number of plates ordered (integer). Print the bill with a 5 rupee packing charge added once.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: plate price and plate count.

Output Format:
Food total: <price * count>
Packing: 5
Bill: <price * count + 5>

Constraints:
1 <= plate price <= 500, 1 <= plate count <= 100

code.title: Temperature Converter
code.description:
A weather dashboard converts Celsius readings to Fahrenheit. Read the temperature in whole degrees Celsius and print the Fahrenheit value with one decimal place.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: temperature in Celsius.

Output Format:
Celsius: <c>
Fahrenheit: <F with exactly one decimal>

Constraints:
-100 <= Celsius <= 100

code.title: Travel Cost Splitter
code.description:
Friends on a trip share the taxi fare equally. Read the total fare (integer rupees) and the number of friends (integer). Print the equal share each friend pays (integer division) and the remainder that the trip leader keeps.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: total fare and friend count.

Output Format:
Each pays: <fare / count>
Leader keeps: <fare % count>

Constraints:
1 <= fare <= 100000, 1 <= count <= 20

code.title: Employee ID Card Formatter
code.description:
The HR system prints ID cards for new joiners. Read the employee name (single word), employee ID (integer) and department (single word), then print the card inside a border of '=' characters.

Input Format:
One line with three tokens: name (single word), employee ID (integer), department (single word).

Output Format:
====================
EMPLOYEE CARD
Name: <name>
ID: <empId>
Dept: <dept>
====================

Constraints:
1 <= employee ID <= 99999
code.sampleoutput2:
====================
EMPLOYEE CARD
Name: Vikram
ID: 107
Dept: ECE
====================

code.title: Gym Membership Bill
code.description:
A fitness studio bills members for a plan. Read the number of months (integer), the monthly rate (integer rupees) and a one-time joining fee (integer rupees). Print the plan cost, the fee and the grand total.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: months, monthly rate, joining fee.

Output Format:
Plan cost: <months * rate>
Joining fee: <fee>
Grand total: <plan cost + fee>

Constraints:
1 <= months <= 36, 100 <= rate <= 20000, 0 <= fee <= 5000

Plan cost: 2500
Joining fee: 1000
Grand total: 3500

Plan cost: 3600
Joining fee: 5000
Grand total: 8600

Plan cost: 10800

Grand total: 10800

code.title: Petrol Pump Receipt
code.description:
A fuel station prints a receipt after refuelling. Read the litres delivered (a double) and the price per litre (a double). Print the litres, the rate and the amount payable, each with exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with two doubles: litres and price per litre.

Output Format:
Litres: <litres, 2 decimals>
Rate: <rate, 2 decimals>
Amount: <litres * rate, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0.5 <= litres <= 200, 50 <= rate <= 200

code.title: Class Test Average
code.description:
A class mentor records three test scores for a student. Read the three integer scores and print the total, the exact average (double with two decimals) and the integer part of the average.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: score1, score2, score3.

Output Format:
Total: <sum>
Average: <average with 2 decimals>
Rounded down: <integer part of average>

Constraints:
0 <= each score <= 100

code.title: Currency Note Split
code.description:
An ATM dispenses cash using the fewest notes of denominations 500, 100, 10 and 1. Read the withdrawal amount (an integer) and print how many notes of each denomination are handed over.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: amount.

Output Format:
500s: <count>
100s: <count>
10s: <count>
1s: <count>

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 100000

code.title: Cafe Tip Calculator
code.description:
A cafe app adds a tip before settling the bill. Read the bill amount (double rupees) and the tip percentage (integer). Print the tip amount and the total, both with two decimal places, plus the whole-rupee total obtained by truncating the decimals.

Input Format:
One line with a double and an integer: bill amount, tip percent.

Output Format:
Tip: <tip, 2 decimals>
Total: <bill + tip, 2 decimals>
Whole rupees: <integer part of total>

Constraints:
1 <= bill <= 100000, 0 <= tip percent <= 50

code.title: Electricity Bill Engine
code.description:
A power distribution company charges domestic consumers by slab:
- first 100 units at 3.50 rupees per unit
- next 200 units (101 to 300) at 5.00 rupees per unit
- units above 300 at 8.00 rupees per unit
A fixed meter rent of 90 rupees is added, and an energy duty of 5 percent is charged on the energy charge (slab cost only).
Read the units consumed (integer) and print the complete bill.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: units consumed.

Output Format:
Units: <units>
Energy charge: <slab cost, 2 decimals>
Meter rent: 90.00
Energy duty: <5% of energy charge, 2 decimals>
Total bill: <sum of all, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0 <= units <= 10000

code.title: Taxi Fare Meter
code.description:
A city taxi computes fares as follows:
- base fare of 40 rupees covers the first 2 km
- every additional km costs 15 rupees (fractional km in input means charge per complete km after the second, rounded down)
- a night trip (flag 'Y') adds a 20 percent surcharge on the running fare (base + distance charge)
- waiting time beyond 5 free minutes costs 2 rupees per minute
Read the distance (double km), the night flag (a single character Y or N) and the waiting minutes (integer), then print the bill.

Input Format:
One line with a double, a character and an integer separated by spaces: distance, night flag, waiting minutes.

Output Format:
Distance km: <distance>
Base fare: 40
Distance charge: <charge>
Night surcharge: <surcharge>
Waiting charge: <charge>
Total: <grand total with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0.0 <= distance <= 500, waiting minutes 0 to 120

code.title: Payroll Slip Generator
code.description:
A startup payroll script produces a monthly slip. Read the employee name (single word) and basic salary (integer rupees). The components are:
- HRA = 15% of basic
- DA = 8% of basic
- PF deduction = 12% of basic
- gross = basic + HRA + DA
- tax = 0 when basic is below 20000, otherwise 10% of (gross - PF)
- net = gross - PF - tax
Print the full slip with every money component shown with two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with a name (single word) and an integer basic salary.

Output Format:
PAYSLIP: <name>
Basic: <basic, 2 decimals>
HRA: <hra, 2 decimals>
DA: <da, 2 decimals>
Gross: <gross, 2 decimals>
PF: <pf, 2 decimals>
Tax: <tax, 2 decimals>
Net pay: <net, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1000 <= basic salary <= 500000
code.output3:
PAYSLIP: Meera
Basic: 1000.00
HRA: 150.00
DA: 80.00
Gross: 1230.00
PF: 120.00
Tax: 0.00
Net pay: 1110.00
code.whitelist: cin, cout, if, else, string, fixed
code.sampleoutput2:
PAYSLIP: Rahul
Basic: 15000.00
HRA: 2250.00
DA: 1200.00
Gross: 18450.00
PF: 1800.00
Tax: 0.00
Net pay: 16650.00

code.title: Fuel Station Cashier
code.description:
A fuel pump cashier settles payment from a prepaid wallet. Read the fuel grade (single character P for petrol or D for diesel), the litres filled (double) and the wallet balance (double). Rates: petrol 108.50 per litre, diesel 94.20 per litre. Bulk discount: petrol gets 2 percent off the fuel value when at least 20 litres are filled; diesel gets 3 percent off when at least 30 litres are filled. The wallet pays the discounted amount; print the change that remains in the wallet. Input Format: One line with a character, a double and a double: grade, litres, wallet balance. Output Format: Fuel:

Rate: Fuel value: Discount: Payable: Wallet change: Constraints: 0.5 <= litres <= 500, 0 <= wallet balance <= 1000000
